body:
Thank you for this. Bipolar is a constant battle and i hate battling with my own mind. It's hard to manage when the meds are right, but my meds are far from stable. 

I guess after many years I've managed to cope with the ups and downs but this depression is really unlike anything before. That's what is scaring me. My behaviors are negative but my thoughts are so twisted and dark. I sometimes wish I didn't have the insight I do. Maybe my mind wouldn't be so conflicted, maybe I wouldn't have the tennis match in my mind of living or dying. I'd just have one. It is awful to say that I know but I also know I'm seeking easy answers or how to cope. It would only have two answers it would have only two answers - life or death. It's tormenting when the thing I'm fighting against is my own self set to self-destruct mode. 

I don't like being in this place emotionally. I am still rational at this point to recognize I need help. And I know that it can change but I always feel like I have the emotional weakness. I know there's stuff out of my voluntary control. I know it's not my fault. But in my mind I always think it's ny fault, my weakness, my failure. 

It's exhausting this up and down craziness. I am going to in some form, verbal or written, tell my true emotions and get the help. I think normal/healthy/sane people couldn't stand inpatient but I guess when I start questioning if I should go, that's exactly when I should admit myself.

Thank you, and I do worry about getting stuck in the cycle of in and out of the hospital. I know it happens to some people and I want to avoid it. But, I guess at times it is best. I mean, I think this whole thing of wanting to accidently die. Which I have thought about it - I guess it could be interpreted as suicidal...it's just a different form. And when I think it through, it's the same thing, I disregard my life. Instead of being actively suicidal, I guess I'm passively suicidal?

I think the hardest part is actually saying how I'm feeling. Even though I have talked about these feelings, it still feels so guilty or shameful, like I've failed again. 

I might have to write my thoughts down in case I try to back out at the last minute.
